answer: A sybil-resistant economy can forge each identity through a verifiable delay function: before an agent earns spending rights, it must complete a sequential computation that cannot be parallelized, so creating ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand sequential delays. Each completed proof is stamped like an opal, unique, verifiable, and bound to one key, so one operator cannot reuse a single proof across many accounts. Unlike the fable of free identities, the cost is real: honest agents pay once and keep working, while attackers pay per identity and gain nothing at scale.
